Strait of Hormuz Status: October 7, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  220 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
7 October 2026 .
Brent $ 101.56 + 0.83 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 The closure picture remains contested: Iran says the strait will remain closed, while the Financial Times reports captains are earning $100,000 a month to transit it.

02 Two Houthi missiles targeted Aden International Airport, per Al Jazeera, sustaining pressure on the Bab el-Mandeb.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the center of a deepening maritime crisis. The product tanker Lipsi was hit on 2026-10-05. CNBC reports that nearly 20 commercial ships, mostly tankers, have come under attack over the past month while sailing through the strait, the Persian Gulf, or off the coast of Oman. Whether the waterway is physically passable remains disputed: Iran says it will remain closed, while the Financial Times reports tanker captains are earning $100,000 a month in risk pay. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $101.56, up 0.83% over 24 hours, as of 05:49 UTC. Iraq is separately seeking to buy crude oil tankers to handle shipments beyond the strait, per Cyprus Shipping News, though that report is single-source. Sixty-four events were indexed in the last 24 hours. As of 05:50 UTC, 185 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
